(C1–C3), T2 maps showing decreasing T2 relaxation times during follow-up. (D1–D3), extracellular volume maps showing progressive expansion of abnormal extracellular volume. (E1–E3), late gadolinium enhancement images showing progression from patchy apical enhancement to diffuse subendocardial-to-mid-wall enhancement with relatively less interventricular-septal involvement, particularly in the basal septum, and increasing measured LGE extent. Red arrowheads highlight representative areas of LGE. CMR, cardiovascular magnetic resonance; ECV, extracellular volume; LGE, late gadolinium enhancement.

panels.rationale: Single parasternal long-axis echocardiogram from a confirmed cardiac-only Danon disease patient (de novo LAMP2 insertion mutation case report). The image visibly demonstrates extreme, symmetric left ventricular hypertrophy with a markedly thickened interventricular septum and left ventricular posterior wall (both 1.4 cm), directly matching the caption's measurements. Colored caliper annotations (blue crosses on the septum, green crosses on the posterior wall, yellow V marker) confirm the finding. Not a diagram, control, or other-disease panel; the manifestation and disease attribution are both clear. [raw subtype: cardiac_only]

panels.rationale: H&E photomicrograph of the postmortem donor heart in a Danon disease article, with the caption explicitly describing extensive vacuolization of cardiomyocytes (arrows). Cardiomyocyte autophagic vacuolization is the classic histopathological hallmark of Danon disease, and the disease attribution is directly supported by the article title and caption. The figure is a real human histopathology image with no third-party copyright indicated.

panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph of the donor's heart from a Danon disease article; caption explicitly describes myocyte hypertrophy and disarray, and in-text reports biventricular hypertrophy. This is a real human postmortem tissue section visibly showing the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy manifestation of Danon disease, so it is included. The normalized finding danon_disease_extreme_myocardial_hypertrophy captures the extreme/biventricular myocardial hypertrophy; the accompanying myocyte disarray is not in the vocabulary and is proposed. No arrows or finding labels are present (only a scale bar).
